items.title: Why Gucci's 'Made in China' sneakers are raising questions
items.summary: Gucci's new Drip sneaker (Demna's first for the house, around AUD/EUR 800) and a slip-on leather model are labelled Made in China, breaking with the brand's Italian-manufacturing heritage. Australian retail trade press quotes Berenberg analysts warning of tension between provenance and luxury positioning, and Milan consultant Simon Whitehouse calling it 'not a good look.' Barclays' Carole Madjo links the move to recent price cuts, questioning whether shoppers should keep buying Gucci as price signals fall. Gucci says Italy stays at the heart of its manufacturing and the Chinese partner was chosen for technical capability.

items.source: Ad Hoc News (German financial wire, via Malakye republish)
items.title: Kering stock falls 1.97% as Gucci recovery remains key investor concern
items.summary: Kering shares fell 1.97% to EUR 209.30, just above its 52-week low, after H1 2026 net income plunged 60% year-on-year to EUR 189 million and Gucci revenue dropped 5% on a comparable basis, with EUR 223 million in restructuring costs. RBC Capital and UBS both cut price targets (RBC: EUR 280 to EUR 260; UBS: EUR 285 to EUR 224), though consensus still implies upside if the turnaround executes. Coverage frames Gucci's weakness, including APAC softness, as the central unresolved question for Kering investors.

items.title: Gucci's official account features Thai stars Billkin and PP Krit from Milan's Store Show
items.summary: Gucci's official social account posted a group photo from the 'Gucci The Store Show' (Milan) featuring Thai ambassadors Billkin and PP Krit alongside Romeo Beckham, Carine Roitfeld and Song Weilong. Japanese entertainment press frames this as Thai stars' global presence being broadcast via Gucci's own channel. This is brand-staged activation coverage (Gucci's own post, descriptive write-up, no independent critical verdict) rather than organic third-party opinion.

items.source: Carousell Luxury Branded Fair (Singapore, via fluf.io/everydayonsales event listings)
items.title: Carousell Luxury Branded Fair (Singapore) sells preloved Gucci alongside Chanel, Dior, LV from S$300
items.summary: Carousell's offline resale fair at The Centrepoint (Orchard Road, 9-11 Oct 2026) listed preloved Gucci pieces such as a Logo Pouch at S$390, a Guccissima top-handle bag at S$600 and an Interlocking G crossbody at S$790, alongside Hermes, Chanel, Dior and LV. Gucci sits in the same affordable secondhand tier as mass-market designer peers rather than being treated as a standout holder of value, a mild signal of softening resale positioning in the SEA secondary market versus hard-luxury houses.

items.title: TikTok shopping videos spark comments on Gucci pricing at Central Phuket
items.summary: TikTok videos showing a shopper buying Gucci items at the Central Phuket mall boutique drew mixed comments: some Thai viewers criticized the purchase as overpriced for a tourist-area store, while other (mostly foreign) commenters were more sympathetic, noting tourist-destination retail tends to carry a premium. Discussion centers on value-for-money perception rather than quality, a mild price/value sentiment signal from an organic SNS thread rather than brand-posted content.

collection_notes: Freshness policy applied strictly: today's window is 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-15 (14-day hard cutoff), with priority given to the last 72 hours/7 days. Extensive searches ran in English, Thai, Indonesian, Vietnamese and Korean across news, SNS and community channels per pool.json gucci_core keywords, covering Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam, Philippines, India and Australia. Mandatory critical-angle searches (price hikes, quality complaints, resale drops, boycotts, 'overrated'/'lost its way', store closures, counterfeit/secondhand chatter, Made in China manufacturing) were run and did surface genuine negative/critical material this cycle, chiefly the Made-in-China sneaker provenance controversy (Inside Retail Australia, picked up from Reuters trade coverage) and the Kering stock/earnings weakness story -- both organic critical coverage, not activation. Several strong leads were excluded for exceeding the 14-day freshness window despite high engagement: the Gucci Spring/Summer 2027 'Store Show' in Milan (21-29 Sept 2026, 5.1M social mentions per Onclusive, Thai ambassadors Billkin/PP Krit/Davika driving 40-65% of celebrity social share) was 17-24 days old; Alia Bhatt 'empty bag'/'chota don' meme backlash tied to the earlier La Famiglia/debut show (Feb-March 2026) was many months old; the Vietnam counterfeit-Gucci seizure stories and the PurseForum Gucci Flora thread were already surfaced and used in prior days' SEA pools (2026-10-11 through 2026-10-13) and/or exceeded the window today. A Harper's Bazaar Singapore critics' review of the SS2026 debut and the Grazia Malaysia/Bagaholicboy La Famiglia Marina Bay Sands launch coverage were confirmed via publish-date verification to be from September-October 2025 (over a year old) and were excluded. Net result: a smaller but verified, cross-channel (news/sns/community) pool with genuine critical-angle balance; positives:negatives roughly even this cycle (no 4:1 skew), so no promotional-bias flag is needed today, though the pool remains thin on volume -- true SNS/community depth for SEA continues to be constrained by what the public web surfaces with verifiable dates and working URLs.
